quickSummary: Four quantum numbers (n, l, m_l, m_s) define an electron's state in an atom. Nodal surfaces are regions where ψ² = 0: Radial nodes = (n - l - 1), Angular nodes = l, and Total nodes = (n - 1).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 The Four Quantum Numbers
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 The Four Quantum Numbers

summaryBox.title: Quantum Numbers Hierarchy
summaryBox.takeaway: n (shell size/energy), l (subshell shape/angular momentum), m_l (spatial orientation), m_s (spin angular momentum).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Solvable solutions to the Schrödinger equation yield three spatial quantum numbers ($n, l, m_l$), and electron spin requires the fourth ($m_s$):

1. **Principal ($n = 1, 2, 3, 4\dots$)**: Determines shell size and major energy level. Max electrons per shell $= 2n^2$; total orbitals $= n^2$.
2. **Azimuthal ($l = 0, 1, 2\dots n-1$)**: Determines subshell geometry ($s, p, d, f$). Orbital Angular Momentum:
$$\mathbf{L = \sqrt{l(l+1)} \frac{h}{2\pi} = \sqrt{l(l+1)} \hbar}$$
Max electrons per subshell $= 2(2l+1)$. Total orbitals $= 2l+1$.
3. **Magnetic ($m_l = -l\dots 0\dots +l$)**: Determines spatial orientation in a magnetic field. Total values $= 2l+1$.
4. **Spin ($m_s = \pm 1/2$)**: Determines intrinsic electron spin orientation. Spin Angular Momentum:
$$\mathbf{S = \sqrt{s(s+1)} \hbar = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \hbar}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Nodal Analysis & Orbital Geometries
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Nodal Analysis & Orbital Geometries
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NODAL CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY
                        
   RADIAL NODES (Spherical)   ──► Radial wavefunction R(r) = 0.
                                  Radial Nodes = n - l - 1
                                  
   ANGULAR NODES (Nodal Planes)──► Angular wavefunction Y(θ,φ) = 0.
                                  Angular Nodes = l
                                  
   TOTAL NODES                 ──► Total Nodes = Radial + Angular = n - 1
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Radial Nodes (Spherical Surfaces)**: $\mathbf{n - l - 1}$.
• **Angular Nodes (Nodal Planes / Cones)**: $\mathbf{l}$.
• **Total Nodes**: $\mathbf{(n - l - 1) + l = n - 1}$.

**Subshell Nodal Matrix**:
• **$1s$ ($n=1, l=0$)**: $0$ radial, $0$ angular, $0$ total nodes.
• **$2s$ ($n=2, l=0$)**: $1$ radial, $0$ angular, $1$ total node.
• **$2p_x$ ($n=2, l=1$)**: $0$ radial, $1$ angular ($yz$-plane), $1$ total node.
• **$3p_x$ ($n=3, l=1$)**: $1$ radial, $1$ angular ($yz$-plane), $2$ total nodes.
• **$3d_{xy}$ ($n=3, l=2$)**: $0$ radial, $2$ angular ($xz$ and $yz$ planes), $2$ total nodes.
• **$3d_{z^2}$ ($n=3, l=2$)**: $0$ radial, $2$ angular (**two conical nodal surfaces** at $\theta = 54.74^\circ$, zero planar nodes!), $2$ total nodes.

quickRevision: Max electrons in shell = 2n²; Total orbitals = n².
Orbital angular momentum L = √(l(l+1)) ℏ (depends strictly on l).
Radial nodes = n - l - 1; Angular nodes = l; Total nodes = n - 1.
3d_z² orbital has 0 planar nodes and 2 conical nodal surfaces.
